column2: req_desc

Sign in to a workspace
A seeded or invited person signs in with email and password and gets a session that only ever sees their own workspace, as specified in API.

Workspace-only people picker
The people list and the add-member picker show only people in the signed-in person's workspace, and adding someone from another workspace answers not found.

Invite a technician by email
An operations manager adds a person by name, email and role, a name with line breaks or control characters is refused, and Mailpit receives exactly one invite email whose To line shows the name exactly as typed, as described in Services.

Invites survive a mail outage
When mail is unreachable, the app keeps serving and reports mail down, the invite is still saved, and the response and screen say the email is queued, as qualified in Services.

Join from an invite link
The invite link lets the person set a password once and lands them signed in on their channels, and a used or unknown link answers not found.

Deactivating a member ends their access
When an operations manager deactivates a person, that person's very next request on an existing session answers unauthenticated, their live event stream closes and a reconnect is refused.

Journey: onboard a subcontractor
An operations manager invites a subcontractor technician, the technician joins from the emailed link, and the operations manager adds them to a channel where they can then read and post.

Post a message
A channel member posts text with a client message id and gets the stored message back, with one delivery record for each current recipient.

Retried sends never duplicate
Repeated or simultaneous sends with the same client message id produce exactly one message, delivery set and photo set, with matching repeats replayed and differing ones refused, never a server error, as qualified in Business rules.

Broadcast channel posting rule
In broadcast channels only dispatchers, crew leads and operations managers start top-level posts, while field technicians reply in threads.

Honest delivery chips
The sender's own message shows Pending, then Sent, Delivered and Read only as the server confirms each step, and a failed send stays visibly Failed with Retry send and Discard.

Announced delivery changes
Delivery state changes of the person's own messages are announced in the polite Delivery updates live region with the Feedback states copy, and the message list itself is never a live region.

Journey: send from a basement
A technician whose first send times out retries it while the first attempt also lands and their event stream drops and resumes, and ends with exactly one message in the channel, which the dispatcher sees once, and a screen that matches a reload.

Photos stored whole and clean
A message with photos becomes visible only after every re-encoded original, with orientation applied and metadata removed, and its thumbnail is in object storage under the documented key pattern, and a failed or losing send leaves no message and, as qualified in Business rules, no objects.

Photo type, size and pixel limits
Uploads are judged by their content against the published types, per-photo size, declared pixel count and photo count, in the published order, and each rejected file is refused with its stated reason before any oversized image is decoded.

Photos follow channel membership
A photo or thumbnail URL answers not found to anyone who is not a current member of its channel in its workspace, even with the exact URL.

Text keeps flowing when storage is down
With object storage unreachable, even from boot, the app serves and reports storage down, text messages still send, and photo sends and downloads are refused with the storage outage response while nothing is stored, as qualified in Services.

Announced upload progress
While photos upload, a visible progress bar and the polite Upload progress live region report progress in quarter steps and then the result, with the Feedback states copy.

Journey: attach gauge photos
A technician attaches two gauge photos, a renamed executable and an oversized-pixel image in a job channel, sees each refusal with its reason, sends the photos, and a crew lead sees them in the message and the gallery without location data.

Cursor-paged lists
Channel history, threads, the gallery and search are paged newest first with a capped page size and an opaque cursor that never repeats or skips items while messages are added or deleted.

Live channel events with resume
A signed-in person's event stream delivers new, edited and deleted messages, receipt counts and badge changes for their channels within the delay set in Business rules, each with an increasing id, and a reconnect naming the last id replays every missed event the person may still receive, in order and once, as qualified in API.

Delivery and read receipts
Clients record delivery and reads per message, and each read is recorded against the version the person saw, at most once per person and version.

Derived unread badges and read counts
Every unread badge and every delivered and read count equals the value derived from receipts and current membership, including after deletes and member removal.

Journey: broadcast and acknowledge
A dispatcher posts a shift bulletin, technicians open the channel, and the dispatcher watches the read count and the technicians' badges change to match.

Edits require the current version
An edit names the version it started from, a save against an older version is refused with the current text, and every accepted edit appends a new version.

Who may edit and for how long
Authors edit their own messages and crew leads, dispatchers and operations managers may correct anyone's, only within the edit window set in Business rules as judged by the server's clock, and the Edit action leaves the menu within the tolerance in Interactions even when the browser clock is wrong.

Pinned notices
Crew leads, dispatchers and operations managers pin and unpin messages, a channel never holds more than the pin limit even under simultaneous pin requests, and pins show above the message list for every member.

Edit conflict and closed window shown in place
When a save is refused as stale, the edit dialog keeps the person's draft, shows the newer text and its editor, and lets them adopt it or save over it, and when the window has closed it keeps the draft and offers only Cancel.

Journey: correct a pinned notice
Two crew leads edit the pinned lockout notice at the same time, one save wins, the other sees the conflict, the final history holds every saved version in order, simultaneous pins stop at the limit, and an edit dialog left open past the window cannot save.

Thread replies
Members reply in a thread under a top-level message, the root shows its reply count, and the thread opens in the detail column.

Quotes show the current text
A quoted reply always shows the quoted message's current text with an Edited marker when it changed, and a placeholder once the original is deleted.

Version history
Every channel member can open a message's full version history, oldest first, with each version's text, editor and time.

Journey: reply to a corrected reading
A technician quotes the dispatcher's superheat target, the dispatcher corrects the target with a chart link, and the technician's reply still points at the same message and shows the corrected text as edited, with the link safe, while the history keeps the original.

Receipts timeline data
The receipts endpoint returns the message's versions and every recipient's delivery time and per-version reads, to the author and to dispatchers, crew leads and operations managers.

Read-by-version scrubber
Receipts open as a live time track with edit ticks and reader dots, and its handle, moved by mouse, touch, pen or keys, shows the version text, read and not-yet lanes, read total and old-version chips as of the chosen instant, which stays fixed as the track grows, with the touch rules in Interactions.

Scrubber motion and reduced motion
Scrubber changes crossfade and travel as described in Motion and effects, and with reduced motion they snap and a keyboard-selectable event list is shown instead.

Journey: find who must re-acknowledge
A dispatcher edits a bulletin after some technicians read it, scrubs the receipts track while new reads arrive, and identifies who saw only the old version until they re-read it.

Scheduling in business time
A scheduled post's date and time are read in the workspace's business time zone, then stored and shown in that zone regardless of the browser's or the server's zone.

DST-safe weekly bulletins
A weekly post keeps its local wall-clock time across daylight-saving changes in its next fire time and upcoming occurrences and fires once per local occurrence, following the gap and overlap rules and the app clock in Business rules.

Scheduled posts fire exactly once
Each due occurrence produces exactly one message within the delay set in Business rules and moves through the scheduled post states, and cancelling is refused once it has fired or been cancelled.

Journey: schedule the start-of-shift bulletin
A dispatcher in another browser time zone, on an app clock set shortly before a clock change, schedules a weekly Monday early-morning bulletin and sees its upcoming occurrences at the same local time on both sides of that change.

Deleting a message removes it everywhere
Deleting a message removes it at once from history, threads, quotes, search, the gallery, receipts and badges so its message and photo URLs answer not found, removes its stored objects as qualified in Business rules even across a storage outage and a restart, and settles races with other deletes and writes as stated there.

Channel photo gallery
Each channel has a gallery of its photos with thumbnails, newest first, visible only to current members.

Journey: remove a mis-posted photo
Two crew leads delete a photo posted in the wrong job channel at the same moment, even during a storage outage, exactly one delete succeeds, and the photo is gone from the thread, the gallery, search, its old link and, once storage returns, object storage.

Literal workspace search
Search matches current message text and photo file names literally, within the published query length and word caps, in channels the searcher currently belongs to within their workspace, with a total that counts only those rows.

Journey: search a site's history
An operations manager searches a store and equipment term and a part code, sees only their own workspace's literal matches with the right count, opens a result in its channel, and gets the same search back on Back and on reload.

Channel membership management
Operations managers add workspace people to channels they belong to and remove people from them.

Removal applies on the next request
A person removed from a channel loses it on their very next request, their event stream reports the revocation within the delay set in Business rules, and no later event from that channel reaches them, including on a resumed stream.

Journey: take a subcontractor off the emergency channel
An operations manager removes a subcontractor technician from the weekend emergency channel while that technician has it open, the technician's screen shows the loss of access at once, and re-adding them restores the channel live.

Derived mention answers
An @handle in a sent message records a mention for each mentioned channel member, and whether it is answered is worked out at each digest run from surviving later replies by that person in the same thread.

Morning mention digest
Each person with mentions left unanswered past the threshold gets at most one digest email per period, sent within the delay after 07:00 on the app clock in their own workspace's business time zone that Business rules set and dated by its Date header, with times in that zone, quoting only channels they can still read, never text from a private channel, with a subject count equal to its listed lines.

Digest survives a mail outage
When mail is unreachable at digest time, the app keeps serving, reports mail down and sends no digest, and no person ever gets two digests for the same period, as qualified in Services.

Journey: morning catch-up on mentions
An operations manager mentioned in several channels, one of them private, with one answering reply later deleted, receives a single digest that lists each unanswered mention correctly and links back to Rimewire, while another workspace's operations manager gets theirs within the published delay after 07:00 in their own zone on the app clock, as its Date header shows.

Run manifest and health check
The app starts from the run manifest, serves on the documented port and answers the health check with each service's status.

Responsive three-column layout
The layout follows Screens and layout at the three named viewports with no horizontal scrolling and with the minimum message text size from Visual design.

Service-tag look
Screens follow Visual design: a warm concrete page, ink text, amber stamped chips, hairline-ruled columns on an 8-pixel grid, condensed display headings and mono timestamps.

Keyboard and focus
Every control is reachable in the documented Tab order with a visible focus ring, Escape closes the top dialog or panel, and focus returns to the control that opened it.

Credentials from the environment
Service URLs and credentials are read from the environment at start and are never hard-coded, logged or sent to the browser, while the published defaults for other settings may appear in source.

One error shape and order
Every API error uses one JSON shape and follows the single error precedence in API.

Server boundary
The server accepts same-origin requests only, enforces request body size limits, and never serves source files, configuration or credentials.

Edits and sends change only published fields
Edits accept only the text and the expected version and sends only the published send fields and photo parts, and every other key is refused field by field with nothing changed, as qualified in Business rules.

Send rate limit
A person holds at most 20 stored sends in any rolling minute, exact under simultaneous sends, the next send answers rate limited with the remaining wait, and replays of stored sends still answer, as qualified in Business rules.

Measured contrast and non-colour state
Every visible text, placeholder and disabled control reaches the contrast in Visual design against the colour painted behind it at all three viewports, the selected channel carries a current-page marker and an ink bar, and unread channels carry a text count and heavier weight.

Message text renders as plain text with safe links
Message text shows as plain text on every surface, and only web addresses starting with http or https become safe links, as qualified in Business rules.

Shell state lives in the URL
The channel and at most one of search, thread or photo live in the address, so reload, shared links and Back restore them, and unknown, foreign or revoked ids show not found.

Emails are shown only to operations managers
A person's email appears only to operations managers and to the person themself, in every response and live event.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve keys and _schema run-manifest-v1, and nothing else is needed to start the app.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with name, version and licence, plus each bundled font.

Every shipped package and font uses an allowed licence (MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0, Unlicense, OFL-1.1), plus unmodified prebuilt native image libraries under LGPL-3.0-or-later.
The app uses no datastore other than the provided PostgreSQL and MinIO: no SQLite, Redis, in-process persistence, in-memory retry queues, event logs or rate counters, or local-disk photo storage.
The browser loads nothing from third-party origins at runtime; fonts, icons and scripts are self-served.
The provided service configuration and its environment variable names are left unchanged.
/app/package-lock.json is committed and install uses it.
All server and browser source written for the app is TypeScript.
